notes: This contract records the portable C++ TCK check for the official IEEE 1516.1 order-type control surface. The source uses only standard C++ RTIambassador and FederateAmbassador APIs plus the standard library; the adapter supplies the provider package, DDM FOM, endpoint, callback configuration, and logical-time implementation. The scenario directly exercises §8.24.4 page-212-l54-11: the prior owner changes an instance attribute to TIMESTAMP, the second publisher requests acquisition, and the prior owner negotiates and confirms divestiture. The new owner, whose class default is explicitly RECEIVE, then timestamp-sends an update; the service returns no retraction handle and the subscriber observes a timestamp-bearing RECEIVE/RECEIVE callback with the exact object, value, and tag. Negotiation, confirmation, acquisition, and ownership state are asserted. It also directly exercises §8.26.4 page-214-l81-20: it observes the FDD-initialized RECEIVE interaction preference, changes one joined federate through TIMESTAMP and back to RECEIVE, verifies future regular and region-qualified sends follow those preferences, and proves a second publisher's TIMESTAMP preference is isolated from the first publisher's change. Page-214-l87-22 is witnessed by a future regular send. These are installed-package API test results, not provider-conformance or interoperability evidence; no provider-specific claim about names, registries, headers, or implementation behavior is made.
